newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico conservatives insist could win congress.
newsitem.headline: Mexico conservatives insist could win congress.

text.p: Shrugging off recent reverses in opinion polls, Mexico's biggest opposition party insisted Wednesday that it still had a chance of winning a majority in the lower house of Congress in crucial elections this July.
Felipe Calderon, leader of the conservative National Action Party (PAN), said his party had a "very solid and growing" position across the country.
"The only party which is disputing the (lower house) majority with the (ruling) Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) is the PAN," Calderon said.
"The PRI will not get an absolute majority in the Chamber of Deputies. That's a basic point," he added.
Mexico votes July 6 for a new lower house of congress, a quarter of the senate and six state governors, as well as the mayor of Mexico City.
Opinion polls show the PRI will be hard pressed to keep its majority in the Chamber of Deputies, the lower house, which it has held uninterrupted since 1929.
But they also show that the PAN, which last year had looked very strong, has been losing ground in recent months to the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).

Trying to put a brave face on recent polls showing his party falling into third place in the Mexico City mayor's race, Calderon said people were "mistaken" to think that the PAN had already been defeated in the capital.
